rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The mushroom is the basidiocarp of a soil mycelium: a stipe with annulus lifting a pileus whose gills carry basidia releasing four exogenous basidiospores each — billions per cap. Edible (*Agaricus*) and deadly (*Amanita*) species are separated by volva, gill and spore colour, cap texture and spore print, but only expert identification is safe.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Agaricus is the edible button mushroom of the course. Amanita includes deadly species. Colour and a pleasant smell are not safe tests. Only a known edible species is food.
Beyond mushrooms, fungi rot dead matter, feed yeast fermentation, provide penicillin, and cause rusts, smuts and skin infections. Mycorrhiza helps tree roots take minerals.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Mushroom vs mycelium:** the mushroom is the temporary reproductive structure; the perennial mycelium in the substrate is the actual fungal body.  ·  **Annulus vs volva:** annulus = ring on the stipe (from the partial veil); volva = cup at the base (from the universal veil) — the volva is the *Amanita* warning sign.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Match the organism to the character.  ·  A product does not move an organism into another kingdom.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Agaricus bisporus*** — the cultivated white mushroom.  ·  ***Morchella*** — the morel, prized wild edible.

rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What is a basidiocarp? **Answer.** The **fruiting body of a basidiomycete** — the mushroom (or bracket, puffball) made of stipe, annulus and pileus — whose gills carry the **hymenial surface lined with basidia**, each basidium producing four **exogenous basidiospores**.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Why billions of spores:** spore-to-mycelium survival odds are tiny; overwhelming numbers are the fungus's evolutionary answer.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Mushroom = basidiocarp: stipe + annulus + pileus with gills bearing basidia → 4 exogenous basidiospores each; billions of spores per cap.  ·  Edible vs poisonous: volva, gill/spore colour (dark vs white), cap texture, spore print, odour — never one character alone.  ·  Beneficial fungi: food (Agaricus, Morchella), yeast fermentation, penicillin, organic acids, enzymes, vitamins, mycorrhiza, research (Neurospora).  ·  Harmful fungi: rusts/smuts/blights, aflatoxin (Aspergillus flavus), mycoses (Candida, ringworm), Amanita poisoning, wood rot.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Mushroom farming converts agricultural waste (straw, manure) into protein.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ***Amanita phalloides*** — death cap; amatoxins; most lethal mushroom.

rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Visible Face of Fungi The mushroom is the only fungus most people ever see — the temporary fruit of a vast hidden mycelium. The Mushroom (*Agaricus*) — Structure ### 2.1 What a mushroom actually is The mushroom is a **basidiocarp** — the fruiting body of a basidiomycete whose true body is the white mycelium ramifying through soil and litter. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Poisonous ≠ brightly coloured:** *Amanita phalloides* can be plain white; identification requires multiple characters.  ·  Economic-importance answers need named examples for every point — lists without examples lose marks.  ·  "The mushroom is a fruit; the fungus is the forest beneath it."

rows.label: More ideas
